claim: For every strictly positive non-equilibrium periodic solution of the spatially homogeneous Gao–Meng delayed phytoplankton–zooplankton–fish model, with period mean denoted by an overbar, the fish equation implies the exact finite-amplitude identity \[\frac{\bar Z}{a+\bar Z}-\frac{g_2}{\gamma_2}(b+\bar F)=\frac{a}{(a+\bar Z)^2}\,\overline{\frac{(Z-\bar Z)^2}{a+Z}}>0.\] Consequently every such cycle satisfies \(0<\bar F<\gamma_2/g_2-b\) and \[\bar Z>\frac{a g_2(b+\bar F)}{\gamma_2-g_2(b+\bar F)}.\] At the paper's numerical coefficients \(a=1/2\), \(b=1/4\), \(\gamma_2=3/40\), \(g_2=1/5\), this becomes \(0<\bar F<1/8\) and \(\bar Z>(1+4\bar F)/(1-8\bar F)\).
integrity: The proof is reconstructed directly from the printed fish equation and exact period integration; symbolic computation is used only as a replayable algebra check.
scientific_limitations: The result is a necessary constraint for strictly positive periodic solutions and does not prove their existence, uniqueness, stability, or period.
The argument is for the spatially homogeneous delayed system and does not cover spatially nonconstant solutions of the reaction-diffusion model.
Two related Crowley–Martin papers were not available in full text during comparison; this access limitation is retained as a residual originality risk.
title: Exact fish-mean ceiling and zooplankton variance defect on Crowley–Martin cycles
